subject: DataBridge renewal — executive approval requested for concession package
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@databridge.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DataBridge renewal — concession request and ask for exec review

Team —

Quick context: DataBridge (current annual commit $220k ARR) is pushing hard on price and SLA for their upcoming renewal (contract end: 2026-11-15). They signaled yesterday that their procurement team will 1) push for 40% off list for year 1, 2) ask for a one-time 3-month bill credit to offset migration hiccups, and 3) require 99.995% SLA for the core inference path (they're in ad-serving pipelines). If they don’t get meaningful relief we risk them moving to a competitor or splitting the workload elsewhere.

What I recommend from a retention POV (minimal acceptable to keep the relationship):
- 30% discount off current list for year 1 only (revert to standard pricing on renewal year 2)
- One-time 3-month service credit applied to first invoice after renewal
- Addendum: SLA guardrail — we add a 99.95% SLA for inference with a capped credit schedule (we can’t accept open-ended indemnities)

Why: LTV and expansion opportunity with DataBridge (they're evaluating broader use across 3 product lines). The churn risk and reference value matter here; legal redlines are limited but procurement has asked for a consolidated concession package.

Impact note: if approved as above, expected TCV keeps ~$180k net new for this renewal year (approx). I attached a short summary and the basic math. Need an expedited exec OK to offer this before procurement begins formal redlines next week.

Attachments: DataBridge_Renewal_Summary.pdf (summary), price_impact_calc.xlsx (margin impact)

Next steps I'd like:
- Vivek: quick sanity check on margin and finance guardrails
- Marissa: sign off operationally or suggest adjustments
- Jonas/Markus: exec approval if we need to go above standard delegation

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15m to walk through.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[d] 415-555-0192 | dylan@redwood.com

Subject: Re: DataBridge renewal — concession request and ask for exec review

Dylan —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. Quick reactions:
- 30% + 3-month credit + SLA uplift is material. We need to quantify margin impact and ensure this doesn't set a precedent for similar-sized customers in the same vertical.
- From RevOps perspective we have a delegation band that allows up to 20% discount + 1 month credit without exec signoff. Anything beyond requires either CRO signoff or finance OK depending on net margin.

Can you send the following by EOD so I can run a quick impact model:
1) current ARR & committed spend line items for the account (breakdown by product)
2) expected 12mo churn assumption with and without concession
3) proposed amend language for the SLA (I want to see the capped credit schedule)

I ran a quick sketch attached (price_impact_calc.xlsx) — if the 30% ask holds we drop below the acceptable gross margin threshold for this rep band.

Standby for a short call if needed.

-Vivek
Finance | Redwood Inference

I appreciate the quick context. My read is: this is a strategic retention — DataBridge is a logo we can reference and they have expansion potential. That said, we need to protect margin and make the concession conditional:
- Authorized: up to 20% discount + one-time 1-month credit (RevOps can approve)
- Anything beyond (30% / 3 months / SLA 99.995%) requires CRO/exec signoff — please escalate.

If we go to execs, present the counter-offer and a succinct risk/reward doc: 1 page max with the churn upside, reference value, expansion roadmap, and concrete rollout milestones + termination triggers. Keep legal redlines minimal and codify the credit mechanics.

Dylan — can you draft the one-pager and the redline for the SLA addendum? Aisha — please prepare the HubSpot deal notes + updated forecast override if we move forward.

Marissa
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: DataBridge renewal — executive approval requested for concession package

Jonas / Markus —

Escalating for formal executive approval. Summary below (short & bolded asks):

Account: DataBridge Analytics (DEAL-4821)
Current ARR: $220k
Renewal date: 2026-11-15
Risk: procurement pushing to move to a competitor; churn would lose reference and expansion motion

Requested concession (customer ask):
- 30% off list for year 1
- One-time 3-month credit applied to first invoice
- SLA addendum to 99.995% for inference with customer-favorable credit ladder

Sales counter (authorized by Marissa):
- RevOps delegation covers up to 20% discount + 1-month credit without exec signoff
- Anything beyond needs exec signoff — this is the ask to you both.

Why we should approve:
- Expansion potential across three product lines; estimated pipeline influence could add $400k ARR in 18 months
- Customer is a strong reference for our ad-serving vertical (high leverage for other deals)
- We can hard-code termination/expansion triggers and a capped SLA credit schedule to limit open exposure

Financial impact if approved (approx):
- Year 1 net: ~$154k (post concessions)
- Gross margin delta: decreased ~18 percentage points vs. current plan (per attached calc)

Requested approvals (choose one):
1) Approve the full concession (30% + 3 months + SLA uplift) — commercial terms go to legal for redline and then to customer for signature.
2) Approve a negotiated middle (25% + 2 months + SLA 99.95%) — sales commits to aggressive expansion plan and measurable milestones.
3) Deny — let renewal proceed to standard pricing and prepare offboarding / transition support.

If you approve (1 or 2), please reply with: APPROVE CONCESSION + preferred option (1 or 2) so RevOps and Legal can prepare amended SOW & DocuSign link. We need the answer by EOD Tue 6 Oct to keep procurement timeline.

Attachments included again: DataBridge_Renewal_Summary.pdf, price_impact_calc.xlsx, redlines_v1.docx

Thanks for the quick review — happy to join a call with the customer if either of you want to hear them directly.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
